target_customer: Families and friends of incarcerated people, who pay to send photos, mail and make cheaper calls
problem: Inmates and families struggle to communicate: digital photos cannot reach prisons and prison phone calls are expensive.
business_model: Consumer pay per use: photos printed and mailed (Fotopigeon, 50 cents per photo), cheaper calls (Telepigeon) and inmate search data

founders.name: Frederick Hutson
education: Brandon High School, Florida (no college degree stated)
founders.background_notes: Former federal inmate convicted on drug charges; idea formed in prison (Wikipedia).

founders.name: Alfonzo Brooks
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; Wikipedia says he employed Hutson during work release.

founders.name: Clifford Keeney
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no bio.

exit.reason: Pigeonly, Inc. filed Chapter 11 in Nevada (case 24-10355) on 2024-01-26 after revenue fell and it could not repay merchant cash advances. The case was still active in January 2025. YC marks it inactive though a founder bio says it still runs.

technical_complexity.rationale: Printing and mailing workflow, facility data aggregation and VoIP calling for inmates, mostly operations and data collection.

defensibility.rationale: A database of inmates and facilities helped, but the service could be copied by other mail and phone providers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found. Later competitors such as Sandboxx, Flikshop and JPay served the same customers. Company filed Chapter 11 in January 2024.

market_need_then: Press in 2015 reported about a million pieces of mail forwarded and about eight million minutes of calls, showing demand from families under high prison phone rates.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven founder story of a former inmate helping families

branding.brand_signature: Pigeon family of products: Fotopigeon and Telepigeon
branding.community_and_virality: Strong founder story press from ABC News, NBC, Complex, Vice and Entrepreneur.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name, product sub brands, and strong human interest coverage of the founder.

outcome_analysis: Pigeonly started in 2013 with a $1M seed, joined YC in Winter 2015 and reached millions of minutes and about a million pieces of mail by 2015 on strong founder market fit. Revenue later dropped and cash flow fell short, so it took merchant cash advances it could not repay, and filed Chapter 11 on January 26, 2024. The company was still alive as a filer when last reported, so inactive status reflects bankruptcy rather than a clean shutdown.
notes: pigeonly.com homepage loaded and shows an active service covering over 4,000 facilities; its about page was not fetched. Totals conflict across databases: CB Insights $3.83M over 13 rounds, Craft $5.1M, Bouncewatch $6.59M, a 2015 article over $2M, Entrepreneur $3.2M, so rounds are missing. The seed date of 2013-09 comes from StartupIntros (an aggregator) and the $1M and investors from Black Enterprise. The August 2019 $750K (Form D style, Fundz) and December 2019 $2M (StartupIntros, labelled Series U) each rest on a single aggregator. Mattermark reports $875K per a regulatory filing, undated and not recorded as it may overlap. VC Beast lists Kapor Capital and Harlem Capital Partners as investors with no round detail. No dated pre-batch competitor source was found, so the list is empty. Exit type is unknown because the bankruptcy outcome is not reported.
